items.title: Jimmy Witherspoon interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, FL, April 12, 1996
items.q: He can often be found in the company of early bandmates Jay McShann and Claude “Fiddler” Williams.

ctx.x: Blues and jazz vocalist Jimmy Witherspoon was born in 1923 and grew up surrounded by Baptist choir music and the blues played by local Arkansas musicians. His musical debut came in the unlikely city of Calcutta during his service in the Merchant Marine. On his return to California, he met Jay McShann and replaced Walter Brown as Jay‘s vocalist. A list of hits followed, including “Ain’t Nobody’s Business” and “Big Fine Girl.” Jimmy has recorded steadily throughout his career and counts his triumph at the 1959…
Jimmy was interviewed by Monk Rowe, Director of the Fillius Jazz Archive, at the Sarasota Jazz Festival on April 12, 1996.
